spec.title: Strict CSP without console errors on every page
spec.goal: Every Operon page logs browser console errors caused by the backend's Content-Security-Policy: the Google Fonts stylesheet (fonts.googleapis.com) is refused, and an inline <script> in frontend/index.html is refused by script-src 'self'. Make every page load with zero console errors while keeping the CSP strict: never add 'unsafe-inline' or 'unsafe-eval' to script-src. Move the inline script into a same-origin module (or remove it if it is redundant) and either self-host the fonts or allow exactly the needed origins (style-src fonts.googleapis.com, font-src fonts.gstatic.com). Add backend tests that check the CSP header forbids inline scripts and allows only the intended font origins, and that the built index.html contains no inline script.
spec.constraints: Keep the CSP strict. Touch only CSP, index.html, the moved script and tests. All backend tests, frontend tests, typecheck, lint and build must pass. Put all code changes (index.html, the moved script, backend CSP, tests) in ONE coder task: they touch the same files, so parallel writers would conflict. Reviewer and security engineer review after it.

findings.title: The CSP test suite fails ("all tests must pass") because the built-index test hard-fails when frontend/dist is absent
findings.observation: _built_index_or_skip() reads scripts/atlas/test-frontend.sh and scripts/atlas/build.sh to decide whether to fail or skip when frontend/dist/index.html is missing. The check requires the literal substring "vite.js build" in build.sh, but build.sh wraps that in the helper line `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build --logLevel warn`; the intended string is therefore never found ("vite/build" is also not matched because test-backend.sh is not consulted for it). In any checkout where the frontend has not been built, the helper takes the fail branch instead of the skip branch, so the whole backend suite fails. The mission requires backend tests to pass; whether they pass here depends on check ordering (frontend-build may run after `tests`). Either way the guard is dead code: its claim "only fail when the frontend build is part of the checks" is not what it does, and if the built index ever disappears the suite reports a red backend instead of the real cause.
findings.recommendation: Match the real command or drop the heuristic: `return "vitest" in command and "vite" in checks` (or check for "vite/bin/vite.js"), or simply skip with a clear message when frontend/dist is missing and keep a separate assertion that the build artefact exists in the frontend-build check. Then the backend suite is green on a clean checkout and the built-index guarantee is still enforced by the build check.
findings.evidence: run_tests → exit 1, log art_aW88x2mAXkCv: "1 failed, 23 passed"; test_built_index_html_has_no_inline_script → Failed: .../frontend/dist/index.html is missing; run scripts/atlas/build.sh first. Cause in the same diff: scripts/atlas/build.sh:4 is `node node_modules/vite/bin/vite.js build --logLevel warn`, which does not contain the substring "vite.js build" that _frontend_test_shipped() searches for (backend/tests/test_csp.py:71).

findings.title: No inline/eval script vector: policy is stricter than the base and the remaining inline style is non-executable
findings.observation: script-src is exactly ["'self'"]: the inline <script> was removed from frontend/index.html in favour of two same-origin module scripts, and no 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', nonce or extra host is added to any directive. This makes the policy strictly stronger than the base, which carried `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'`: injected or stored <script>/<style> now needs a prior same-origin script compromise. The remaining inline <style> is not governed by script-src; its only effect is the #root opacity guard, and no code in this repository injects style markup (no innerHTML, dangerouslySetInnerHTML, eval or new Function anywhere in frontend/src, frontend/package-lock.json or backend). One residual unknown I could not settle in the sandbox: node_modules is not materialised here, so a runtime style injection inside node_modules (a framework CSS-in-JS runtime) would have been invisible to static reading; the browser_qa flows / and /cases and /analyze and /supervisor with failOnConsoleErrors=true detect it empirically.
findings.recommendation: None required. If a future page needs inline styles, use a nonce for inline <style> rather than re-adding style-src 'unsafe-inline', and keep script-src at 'self'.
findings.evidence: Original header: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; ...` (backend/security.py, removed lines). New value: backend/security.py:35-39. No 'unsafe-inline'/'unsafe-eval' in any directive (grep backend, frontend/src, frontend/index.html → exit 1, log art_Xci2deByaGBK). The only inline <style> is frontend/index.html:13-21 (the #root FOUC guard); its visual effect is reproduced by bootstrap.ts revealApp() and cleared by the 1s animation even if that module 404s (new lines 18-21), plus revealApp() again in main.tsx:8.

findings.title: Font origins are minimal and cannot enable script execution; only residual risk is third-party stylesheet/CSS exfiltration
findings.observation: style-src gets fonts.googleapis.com only, font-src gets fonts.gstatic.com only (plus 'self' and data:), and neither directive inherits the other's origin because default-src stays 'self' and both are spelled out explicitly. Keys and responses (unsafe-inline, unsafe-eval) can no longer be fetched from any origin, and no directive that can execute or fetch data was widened: script-src 'self', connect-src 'self', img-src 'self' data:, object-src 'none', frame-ancestors 'none', base-uri 'self', form-action 'self'. A stylesheet from fonts.googleapis.com cannot execute script under script-src 'self', and an attacker-influenced font origin cannot be reached because the origins are fixed constants, not derived from a request header or config. The one cross-origin dependency added beyond the mission's ask is style-src (the stylesheet itself, unavoidable if the <link> stays): it means a compromise of fonts.googleapis.com could inject CSS, which cannot run script here, and the stylesheet could exfiltrate same-origin text through url() requests to fonts.gstatic.com. Minor in impact (the request goes to Google, which already receives the page request context) but it is the reason self-hosting the two fonts remains the stronger option.
findings.recommendation: If the cross-origin CSS dependency is unwanted, download the Inter/JetBrains Mono woff2 files into frontend/public and drop the three font <link>s plus both origins from the policy; then every page is fully same-origin. Also add Subresource Integrity to the stylesheet <link> if the CDN URL is kept (it pins the exact bytes Google serves today).
findings.evidence: backend/security.py:29-30 and :37 (origins), :35 'default-src 'self'', :38 img-src 'self' data:, connect-src 'self'; backend/tests/test_csp.py:100-118 asserts each directive's remote origins equal exactly one expected Google origin and that style-src/font-src do not swap. frontend/index.html:9-10 pins the two preconnect targets and only line 11 loads fonts.googleapis.com; the CSS it returns points at fonts.gstatic.com, the only other origin loaded. grep for 'fonts.g' across frontend/index.html, frontend/src, frontend/public → only those lines (log art_qd3sbdBvBV6Q).

findings.title: Inline-script removal does not regress initialization; the only unguarded localStorage write left is in ThemeBootstrap (pre-existing, now inconsistent with bootstrap.ts)
findings.observation: The moved script reproduces the removed inline script's job (clearing the #root FOUC guard) and adds the theme pin that main.tsx alone did not do before the first paint. Residual, pre-existing and non-security: ThemeBootstrap.tsx still calls localStorage.setItem unguarded in an effect, so where storage is blocked (Safari private mode, storage partitioning) React logs an uncaught SecurityError/QuotaExceededError — that would break the mission's zero-console-errors goal on those browsers. bootstrap.ts also writes the persisted key before ThemeBootstrap mounts, so a stored/URL theme is applied consistently and cannot be left unresolved; with an unreadable storage the key is simply absent, the guard is still cleared by the 1s animation fallback, and index.html keeps an explicit dark background.
findings.recommendation: Wrap the two localStorage writes in ThemeBootstrap.tsx (:11 read, :17 write) in the same try/catch pattern bootstrap.ts uses, or route them through the exported storedTheme/persistTheme helpers so there is one guarded accessor.
findings.evidence: bootstrap.ts:21-27 (try/catch around localStorage; in private mode the stored value is only a preference and retrieval failure is tolerated). store/index.ts defaults theme:'dark'. ThemeBootstrap.tsx:10-19: an initial useEffect reads localStorage('sentinel-theme') and calls set({theme: saved}), and a second useEffect writes localStorage.setItem('sentinel-theme', theme) on every theme change without a try/catch. frontend/index.html:15-16 still sets background #0A0A0A, and bootstrap.ts:57-60 sets dataset.theme before first paint.

findings.title: font-src keeps `data:` — broader than the stated minimal font allowance, justification not verifiable from the repository
findings.observation: The task asks for a minimal font-origin allowance, and data: is broader than the stated need ('the two Google Fonts origins'). A data: font is a possible smuggling channel: a data:text/html resource loaded as a font in some engines, or a resource the CSP explicitly relaxes for a URL scheme an attacker can embed in markup/JS. I could not show an exploitable path here — no data: font exists in the repository, script execution is blocked by script-src 'self', and I could not read node_modules (not materialised) to rule out a library that loads fonts from data: URIs.
findings.recommendation: If no data: font is actually loaded (nothing in frontend/public or the CSS does), drop `data:` from font-src to match the documented minimal set; otherwise document the specific inlined font in the policy comment. Keep the existing test that pins the directive to exactly one remote origin.
findings.evidence: backend/security.py:38 keeps `font-src 'self' data: ...`. grep for data: URIs over frontend/index.html, frontend/src and frontend/public matched only the policy itself (log art_dSGxvHD5BqvN); no `src="data:"` font or exists in the sources, and the base policy already had data: in font-src/img-src. frontend/node_modules is absent in this sandbox (ls → exit 1, log art_xRpG2vC9vACs), so third-party runtime data: usage could not be read.

findings.title: test_csp.py is order-dependent: its built-index test fails whenever the pytest run starts before a frontend build exists
findings.observation: `test_built_index_html_has_no_inline_script` reads frontend/dist/index.html and, when the file is missing, `pytest.fail`s (it only skips when neither vitest nor `vite build` is wired into the scripts). frontend/dist is a git-ignored build artifact that a fresh worktree/checkout does not contain. Running the acceptance command for this task — the backend suite — in the worktree as it stands (no dist/) fails: 1 failed, 23 passed, with `Failed: .../frontend/dist/index.html is missing; run scripts/atlas/build.sh first`. The acceptance criterion "Backend and frontend test, typecheck, lint and build commands pass" is therefore only met when the build happens to have run first in the same worktree, which the reviewer ran only after the failing run.
findings.recommendation: Make the check independent of run order: assert the property against the Vite template itself (frontend/index.html already is the built page's template, and the coder's `test_frontend_index_has_no_inline_script` covers it), and treat a missing dist/index.html as `pytest.skip` instead of `pytest.fail` — or, if the built artifact must be asserted, skip cleanly and let the csp-tests/CI stage build before running the backend suite (add the build to scripts/atlas/test-backend.sh or run it from the gate). Do not leave a suite that is red on a clean checkout.
findings.evidence: run_tests at head commit a4b1e50+ (no frontend/dist present): "1 failed, 23 passed in 6.28s", FAILED backend/tests/test_csp.py::test_built_index_html_has_no_inline_script — backend/tests/test_csp.py:77 pytest.fail(message). Log art_EuQBBDG5u7sm. The gate script used by the project, scripts/atlas/test-backend.sh, runs `pytest` for the whole suite with no build step.

findings.title: Misleading comment above CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY
findings.observation: The comment "Scripts and connections stay same-origin: no inline stylesheet or script is relied on, so 'self' covers both." sits directly above a policy whose style-src is not same-origin ('self' + fonts.googleapis.com), so the rationale text does not read as intended. The policy itself is correct and strict; only the wording misleads.
findings.recommendation: Reword, e.g. "Scripts and XHR stay same-origin; styles and fonts keep 'self' and add exactly the two Google Fonts origins that index.html uses."
findings.evidence: Diff: backend/security.py CONTENT_SECURITY_POLICY is `f"default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' {GOOGLE_FONTS_STYLE_ORIGIN}; ..."`; the removed header literal had exactly `"default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'; style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; ..."`, so the only real change is `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` -> `style-src 'self' https://fonts.googleapis.com` and `font-src 'self' data:` -> `font-src 'self' data: https://fonts.gstatic.com`.

findings.title: Preconnect hints are only weakly covered by CSP tests; browser-level console cleanliness not reproduced by me
findings.observation: I could not establish that a preconnect to an origin absent from the CSP produces a console error, and no origin was added to connect-src for fonts.gstatic.com. The two errors named in the objective (stylesheet from fonts.googleapis.com via style-src, font binaries from fonts.gstatic.com via font-src) are covered by the header. The stylesheet preconnect lacks `crossorigin`, which at worst wastes one preconnect for a CORS-mode fetch. I could not verify any of this in a browser: process_start with serve:true needs an approval that was not granted in this mission, so "zero console errors on every page" is unverified by me.
findings.recommendation: Optionally add `crossorigin` to the fonts.googleapis.com preconnect. The real check belongs to the csp-browser-qa task: load the backend-served app and confirm the console is empty. If that task cannot run, report the browser-level criterion as unverified rather than inferring it from the header tests.
findings.evidence: frontend/index.html line 26: `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com" />` (no crossorigin) and line 27 `<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.gstatic.com" crossorigin />`. `grep -rn fonts.gstatic.com frontend backend` shows the only usages are these preconnects plus the CSP/security constants, which do allow the font origin. A preconnect is not gated by connect-src in the fetch spec, so no console error is expected; I could not test it in a browser here.
